papers.title: Earth-Abundant 3d Transition Metal-Catalyzed Enantioselective C-H Functionalization
papers.did: Reviews recent progress in enantioselective C-H functionalization catalyzed by earth-abundant 3d transition metals, covering both inner-sphere and outer-sphere mechanisms.
papers.used: Literature review categorized by metal/ligand catalytic system and by type of C-H functionalization reaction.
papers.why: Consolidates strategies for replacing precious-metal catalysts with cheaper, more abundant 3d metals in asymmetric synthesis.
papers.anchor_quote: This review summarizes the rapid progress in 3d metal-catalyzed enantioselective C-H functionalization up to March 2025, encompassing both inner-sphere and outer-sphere mechanisms.

papers.title: Pd(II)-Catalyzed Oxidative Annulation of Alkenes toward Isoxazoline N-Oxides
papers.did: Developed a Pd(II)-catalyzed [3+2] annulation of alkenyl amides and nitroalkanes.
papers.found: The method furnishes isoxazoline N-oxide products in a single step, proceeding with high diastereoselectivity for internal and alpha-functionalized olefins.
papers.used: Pd(II) catalysis with alkenyl amide and nitroalkane substrates.
papers.why: Provides expedient, single-step access to an underexplored heterocycle class with multiple stereogenic centers.
papers.anchor_quote: The method furnishes intricately functionalized isoxazoline N- oxide products in a single step from simple starting materials, enabling expedient access to this underexplored class of heterocycles.

papers.title: Catalytic Functionalization of Unactivated π-Bonds Enabled by Bidentate Directing Auxiliaries
papers.did: Reviews progress in transition-metal-catalyzed functionalization of unactivated pi-bonds using bidentate directing auxiliary strategies across Pd, Ni, and Cu catalysis.
papers.used: Literature review of hydrofunctionalization, difunctionalization, and C-H activation reactions enabled by chelated directing-group intermediates.
papers.why: Consolidates design principles governing reactivity and selectivity to guide future catalyst and ligand design.
papers.anchor_quote: A key feature of this strategy is the formation of chelated intermediates where the bidentate directing auxiliary, tethered to the alkene or alkyne substrate, coordinates strongly to the transition metal catalyst.

papers.title: High-throughput ligand diversification to discover chemical inducers of proximity
papers.did: Used sulfur(VI) fluoride exchange-based high-throughput chemistry to decorate ENL and BRD4 ligands with 3,163 diverse building blocks and screened the analogs for degrader activity.
papers.found: Identified dHTC1, an ENL degrader that recruits the CRL4-CRBN complex, and dHTC3, a molecular glue that selectively dimerizes BRD4 bromodomain 1 to SCF-FBXO3.
papers.used: Sulfur(VI) fluoride exchange (SuFEx) high-throughput chemistry; degrader activity screening.
papers.why: Introduces a scalable, systematic method to discover new chemical inducers of proximity for targeted protein degradation.
papers.anchor_quote: This revealed dHTC1, an ENL degrader that recruits CRL4 CRBN complex through an extended interface of protein-protein contacts and only engages CRBN after pre-forming the ENL:dHTC1 complex.

papers.title: Mechanistically Guided Functionalization of α,α-Disubstituted Alkenyl Amides Enabled by a Conformationally Flexible Directing Auxiliary
papers.did: Used kinetic, organometallic, and DFT studies to identify the reactivity barrier in Pd(II)-catalyzed functionalization of alpha,alpha-disubstituted alkenes, then designed a more flexible directing auxiliary to overcome it.
papers.found: Switching from the rigid 8-aminoquinoline auxiliary to a flexible 2-pyridylmethylamine auxiliary gave a 115-fold rate increase for the model substrate and broadened the scope to sterically encumbered alkenes.
papers.used: Pd(II) catalysis; 8-aminoquinoline and 2-pyridylmethylamine directing auxiliaries; kinetic, organometallic, and DFT studies.
papers.why: Expands access to structurally complex, lipophilic scaffolds from readily available alkenes via mechanistically informed directing-group design.
papers.anchor_quote: This mechanistically informed approach led to a 115-fold rate increase for the model α,α-dimethyl substrate and broadens the scope to sterically encumbered alkenes, including α-spiro(hetero)cyclic systems, with tolerance for diverse N-H and C-H nucleophiles.

papers.title: B-Alkyl-borabicyclo[3.3.1]nonane Reagents Promote Closed-Shell Nickel-Catalyzed Alkylarylation Toward Encoded Cyclooctene Monomers
papers.did: Developed a nickel-catalyzed alkylarylation of 1,5-cyclooctadiene using alkyl-9-BBN reagents as transmetalating agents to maintain a polar reaction mechanism.
papers.found: The method provides 5,6-alkylarylated cyclooctenes suitable for ring-opening metathesis polymerization; DFT showed destabilization of the pretransmetalation complex promotes alkyl-9-BBN reactivity.
papers.used: Nickel catalysis; alkyl-9-BBN transmetalating reagent; DFT calculations; ring-opening metathesis polymerization.
papers.why: Enables access to new tailored cyclooctene monomers for polymer materials with tunable properties.
papers.anchor_quote: This work describes a two-electron redox manifold for the nickel-catalyzed alkylarylation of 1,5-cyclooctadiene and discloses B -alkyl-borabicyclo-[3.3.1]-nonane (alkyl-9-BBN) as an effective transmetalating reagent for maintaining a polar reaction mechanism.

papers.title: Ni(DQ)2: A Useful Gateway to Zero-Valent Nickel Complexes
papers.did: Synthesized Ni(DQ)2 (DQ = duroquinone) from Ni(II) and Ni(0) precursors, guided by DFT calculations.
papers.found: Ni(DQ)2 undergoes facile ligand exchange with phosphine, bis-nitrogen, and diene ligands, and serves as an air-stable precatalyst effective in cases where Ni(COD)(DQ) is not.
papers.used: Duroquinone ligand chemistry; DFT calculations; precatalyst synthesis and ligand exchange.
papers.why: Provides a convenient, air-stable Ni(0) source for organometallic synthesis and catalysis.
papers.anchor_quote: As a precatalyst, Ni(DQ) 2 is found be a competent air-stable precursor for emerging methodology where Ni(COD)(DQ) is ineffective (COD = 1,5-cyclooctadiene).

papers.title: Equivalent Atrop- and Positional Isomerism in Styrene Derivatives Prepared by Enantioselective 1,3-Diarylation
papers.did: Used a combined palladium/amino acid cocatalyst system to convert ortho-alkenyl benzaldehydes into substituted styrenes via successive Mizoroki-Heck arylation.
papers.found: The products display equivalent atrop- and positional isomerism; DFT calculations show atroposelectivity arises from stereoselective beta-H elimination and that Z-product formation is thermodynamically driven.
papers.used: Palladium/amino acid cocatalysis; Mizoroki-Heck arylation; DFT calculations.
papers.why: Reveals a rare coexistence of multiple isomerism forms, deepening understanding of stereocontrol in metal-catalyzed alkene functionalization.
papers.anchor_quote: Here, we report that a simple combination of palladium and amino acid cocatalysts converts ortho -alkenyl benzaldehydes into substituted styrenes possessing equivalent atrop- and positional isomerism.

papers.title: Cu(II)-Catalyzed Hydrofunctionalization of Unactivated Alkynes via π-Lewis Acid Activation
papers.did: Developed a copper(II)-catalyzed stereodivergent hydrooxygenation of unactivated alkynes with carboxylic acids and other O/N-nucleophiles.
papers.found: The method affords trisubstituted E- or Z-alkenes with enol ester functionality with high selectivity, with the syn/anti pathways supported by mechanistic and DFT studies.
papers.used: Cu(II) catalysis; bidentate auxiliary; DFT calculations.
papers.why: Provides a general, selective route to enol ether, enamine, and beta-lactam building blocks from unactivated alkynes.
papers.anchor_quote: A copper(II)-catalyzed stereodivergent hydrooxygenation of electronically unactivated alkynes with carboxylic acids is reported.

papers.title: Harnessing Multi-Center-2-Electron Bonds for Carbene Metal-Hydride Nanocluster Catalysis
papers.did: Used a bottom-up approach leveraging metal-metal multi-center bonds to synthesize a cyclic(alkyl)amino carbene copper-hydride nanocluster.
papers.found: The [(CAAC)6Cu14H12][OTf]2 cluster shows superior stability compared to Stryker's reagent; DFT shows enhanced stability stems from hydride-to-ligand backbonding with the pi-accepting carbene.
papers.used: N-heterocyclic/cyclic(alkyl)amino carbene ligands; copper-hydride nanocluster synthesis; DFT calculations.
papers.why: Provides a bench-stable, efficient copper-hydride precatalyst alternative for catalytic applications.
papers.anchor_quote: This new cluster emerges as an efficient and selective copper-hydride pre-catalyst, thereby providing a bench-stable alternative for catalytic applications.

papers.title: Palladium Bisphosphine Monoxide Complexes: Synthesis, Scope, Mechanism, and Catalytic Relevance
papers.did: Examined internal redox reactions of Pd(II)(bisphosphine)X2 complexes to access and characterize bisphosphine monoxide (BPMO) precatalysts.
papers.found: Characterized a series of Pd(II)(BPMO)(R)(X) oxidative addition complexes bearing 24 different BPMO ligands by NMR and X-ray crystallography, revealing catalytic performance differences from bisphosphine analogs.
papers.used: NMR spectroscopy; X-ray crystallography; organopalladium oxidative addition complexes.
papers.why: Establishes BPMO oxidative addition complexes as a diagnostic tool for developing new catalytic reactions.
papers.anchor_quote: In particular, a series of Pd II (BPMO)(R)(X) (R = aryl, alkyl; X = I, Br) oxidative addition complexes bearing 24 different BPMO ligands were characterized by NMR and X-ray crystallography.

papers.title: High-throughput diversification of protein-ligand surfaces to discover chemical inducers of proximity
papers.did: Used sulfur(VI)-fluoride exchange-based high-throughput chemistry to decorate ENL and BRD4 ligands with 3,163 diverse building blocks and screened the crude products for degrader activity.
papers.found: Identified dHTC1, a potent, stereochemistry-dependent ENL degrader, plus two structurally distinct BRD4 degraders including dHTC3, a molecular glue that dimerizes BRD4 bromodomain 1 to SCF-FBXO3.
papers.used: SuFEx-based high-throughput chemistry; degrader activity screening.
papers.why: Establishes a prospective, target-directed approach to discover molecular glue degraders rather than relying on serendipity.
papers.anchor_quote: Envisioning a prospective approach to discover molecular glues for a pre-selected target, we hypothesized that pre-existing ligands could be systematically decorated with chemical modifications to empirically discover protein-ligand surfaces that are tuned to cooperatively engage another protein interface.

papers.title: Hemilabile and Redox-Active Quinone Ligands Unlock sp3-Rich Couplings in Nickel-Catalyzed Olefin Carbosulfenylation
papers.did: Developed a nickel-catalyzed three-component 1,2-carbosulfenylation of unactivated alkenes with organoboron nucleophiles and alkylsulfenamide electrophiles.
papers.found: Catalyst loadings as low as 1 mol% are achieved; DFT shows the duroquinone ligand adopts different coordination modes (capping, redox-active radical anion, and L-type) at different stages of the catalytic cycle.
papers.used: Nickel catalysis; duroquinone (DQ) hemilabile redox-active ligand; DFT calculations.
papers.why: Reveals a new ligand design principle, hemilabile redox-active quinones, that enables otherwise inaccessible sp3-rich cross-couplings.
papers.anchor_quote: Key to the development of this transformation is the identification of quinones as a family of hemilabile and redox-active ligands that tune the steric and electronic properties of the metal throughout the catalytic cycle.

papers.title: Anti-selective Cyclopropanation of Nonconjugated Alkenes with Diverse Pronucleophiles via Directed Nucleopalladation
papers.did: Developed a directed nucleopalladation reaction of nonconjugated alkenes with diverse pronucleophiles to form densely functionalized cyclopropanes.
papers.found: The reaction gives excellent yields and good anti-selectivity using I2 and TBHP oxidants, including with internal alkenes that are normally challenging substrates for cyclopropanation.
papers.used: Pd-catalyzed directed nucleopalladation; I2/TBHP oxidants; DFT calculations and mechanistic experiments.
papers.why: Provides controlled access to densely functionalized, multiply-substituted cyclopropanes from previously challenging alkene substrates.
papers.anchor_quote: Internal alkenes, which are generally challenging substrates in other cyclopropanation methods, provide excellent yields and good diastereoselectivity in this methodology, allowing for controlled access to cyclopropanes substituted at all three C atoms.

papers.title: Diversification of Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Processes: Taking the Plunge into the Non-PGM Catalyst Pool
papers.did: Reviews recent applications of non-platinum-group-metal (non-PGM) catalysts in pharmaceutical manufacturing processes.
papers.used: Literature review of non-PGM catalytic processes with historical context on platinum-group-metal cost and availability.
papers.why: Highlights the potential of non-PGM catalysis to reduce reliance on costly platinum group metals in drug manufacturing.
papers.anchor_quote: This review covers recent highly relevant applications of non-PGM catalysts in the modern pharmaceutical industry.

papers.title: Stereodivergent, Kinetically Controlled Isomerization of Terminal Alkenes via Nickel Catalysis
papers.did: Developed a nickel-catalyzed platform for stereodivergent, E/Z-selective one-carbon transposition of terminal alkenes into internal alkenes.
papers.found: The reaction proceeds at room temperature using commercial reagents, with distinct catalyst-formation pathways producing the Z- versus E-selective active catalysts; ligand sterics and denticity control stereochemistry and prevent over-isomerization.
papers.used: Nickel catalysis; Ni-H-mediated insertion/elimination mechanism; commercial reagents and additives.
papers.why: Provides a scalable, general route to valuable internal alkenes from terminal alkene feedstocks, overcoming prior generality and scalability limitations.
papers.anchor_quote: Here, we report a nickel-catalyzed platform for the stereodivergent E/Z-selective synthesis of internal alkenes at room temperature.

papers.title: Nickel-Electrocatalytic Decarboxylative Arylation to Access Quaternary Centers
papers.did: Developed a nickel electrocatalytic method for decarboxylative arylation that couples tertiary alkyl fragments to (hetero)aryl halides.
papers.found: Mechanistic studies including cyclic voltammetry and control reactions show the reaction proceeds via a Ni(I)-Ni(II)-Ni(III)-Ni(I) catalytic cycle, ruling out Ni(0) involvement; the method was scaled up in both batch and flow.
papers.used: Nickel electrocatalysis; pyridine additive; cyclic voltammetry and titration experiments.
papers.why: Provides a general, chemoselective method for forming quaternary carbon centers useful for building bioactive molecules in drug discovery.
papers.anchor_quote: Our preliminary mechanistic studies ruled out the involvement of Ni(0) species in this electrochemical cross-coupling, which is mediated by Ni(I) species via a Ni(I)-Ni(II)-Ni(III)-Ni(I) catalytic cycle.

papers.title: Benchtop Nickel Catalysis Invigorated by Electron-Deficient Diene Ligands
papers.did: Chronicles the development of air-stable Ni(0) precursors based on the Ni(COD)(EDD) framework as replacements for air- and temperature-sensitive Ni(COD)2.
papers.found: The precatalysts show reactivity equivalent or enhanced compared to Ni(COD)2 across C-C and C-N couplings, borylations, and C-H activations, and enabled previously inaccessible C(sp3)-S(alkyl) couplings and metallonitrenoid carboamination.
papers.used: Electron-deficient diene (EDD) ligands; Ni(COD)(DQ) precatalyst toolkit; DIBAL-H reduction and electrochemical synthesis.
papers.why: Provides practical, air-stable Ni(0) catalyst tools that broaden accessible reactivity in everyday nickel catalysis.
papers.anchor_quote: By incorporating the precatalyst toolkit into reaction discovery campaigns, our laboratories have been able to perform C(sp 3 )-S(alkyl) couplings and metallonitrenoid carboamination, both of which represent challenging transformations that were inaccessible with traditional phosphine, nitrogen, or electron-deficient olefin ligands.
